own_solution.law: Independent exponential decay gives A1(t)=2400*2^(-t/6) and A2(t)=500*2^(-t/72), with t in hours. Common nonzero detection efficiency cancels, giving t=(72/11)*log2(2400/500). An extra activity q added at preparation replaces 500 by 500+q.
assumptions: Count rates are expected decay count rates.
Both isotopes follow independent exponential decay.
The common detection efficiency is nonzero.
Using 500+q as the initial longer-lived activity requires addition at preparation.

uncertain_fields: The addition time in T45EB is unspecified.

defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: T45EB omits the addition time, whereas its wiring and certified answers require addition at preparation.

counterexamples: For T45EB, adding the 170 Bq batch at preparation gives equality at 12.0489 h; adding it at 24 h leaves equality at 14.8126 h, before the addition.
notes: The base equation, dimensions and numerical precision are correct. For T7283, the certified answers at 110, 170 and 360 Bq are correct; the identical T45EB answers hold only under the unstated preparation-time interpretation. Both efficiency cancellations and all disconnected classifications hold. The explicitly claimed minimal pairs preserve 170 Bq and change the attachment as intended. I withdraw pass 1's rendering_not_minimal flag because pass 2 identifies T9D9A and TF3A2 as deliberate numeral-free controls, rather than number-preserving minimal pairs. No other information was consulted.
